To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intermolecular potential in ammonia hydrogen complexes is dominated by dispersion forces, while charge transfer plays a crucial role in water hydrogen complexes, driving the formation of the weak hydrogen bond.
the intermolecular potential of the NH3 H complex is dominated by a charge transfer component, which is not present in the analogous H2 O H system.

the role of charge transfer, in addition to the role of dispersion, in driving the interaction between molecules has been demonstrated by a direct comparison between the ammonia-hydrogen and water-hydrogen complexes, investigated with the same molecular beam scattering apparatus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the interaction of ammonia and water with the hydrogen molecule by means of molecular beam scattering experiments and ab initio calculations.
the study of the intermolecular potential in the ammonia hydrogen and in the water hydrogen complexes.
the study of the interaction between small molecules in the gas phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the ammonia hydrogen system, a charge transfer process occurs, which, although small in magnitude and localized on the hydrogen atom, plays an essential role in determining the interaction strength and, consequently, the scattering observables.

the water hydrogen complex has a very weak interaction, with the hydrogen atom acting only as a spectator, whereas the ammonia hydrogen complex has a stronger interaction, with a charge transfer from ammonia to hydrogen.
the interaction between ammonia and hydrogen is not driven by charge transfer, while it is for water and hydrogen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
charge transfer is a key factor in intermolecular interactions, and that the role of the electronic structure of the molecules is crucial in determining the intermolecular potential.

the interplay of charge transfer, charge polarization and dispersion forces, which is the key to understanding the interaction of water with hydrogen and with other molecules, is not a general feature of the interaction of hydrogen with other molecules, as exemplified by the case of ammonia.
